cost_model_summary: Customer asked for per-token economics under reserved capacity. Redwood draft assumptions: baseline plan = 8x A100-80GB equiv GPUs reserved; forecast workload mix: 60% embeddings/rerank (batch), 30% chat low-latency, 10% offline scoring. Utilization assumptions: conservative 40% avg, baseline 60% avg, aggressive 80% avg. Amortized infra+license cost per reserved GPU (annual) modeled at $120k/GPU/year (incl. hosting, network, support). Under baseline (8 GPUs @ 60% utilization) effective active-GPU-hours are 8 * 0.6. Tokens/sec assumptions: typical chat instance ~40 tokens/sec per GPU for long-context models; embedding batch throughput ~150k tokens/sec aggregate across GPUs when batched. Resulting blended unit cost per 1k tokens: conservative ~= $0.48, baseline ~= $0.22, aggressive ~= $0.12 (these include reserved amortization but exclude per-request SaaS fees). Customer wants sensitivity table showing rate vs utilization and commit discount tiers.
reserved_capacity_plan: Redwood recommended three commit bands for procurement negotiation: 1) Small reserve: 4 GPUs reserved, 20% burst to shared pool, target ARR ~ $300k; lower commit discount (10%) but lower fixed spend. 2) Mid reserve (recommended for POC->prod): 8 GPUs reserved, 2:1 burst allowed, target ARR ~ $600k; expects 50-70% utilization on steady state, estimated blended token cost $0.18-$0.25 per 1k tokens. 3) Large reserve: 16 GPUs reserved, dedicated throughput with <5% cross-tenant bursting, target ARR > $1M; assumes negotiate SLA with p95 latency targets and higher uptime SLA. Also proposed quarterly utilization reports and an automated rightsizing review every 3 months to adjust commit for next term.
notes:
CRM notes / call highlights:
- Value props that resonated: predictable throughput and clear unit economics, automated KV/prefix caching, model fallback policies for graceful degradation.
- P95 latency target required for trading chat: <= 120ms end-to-end (customer measures at app layer). P50 target 30-50ms. Customer emphasized consistent tail latency during market open spikes.
- Usage profile provided: daily peak QPS at market open ~1.2k requests, average req size 800 tokens (chat + retrieval). Embedding batch windows overnight: ~100M tokens/day.
- Procurement concern: they want a clear breakpoint where reserved capacity beats pay-as-you-go — finance asked for a 3-year NPV comparison and washout period.
- Security: must support customer-managed KMS (HSM preferred) and SAML SSO. Data residency for EU customers (they have EU clients) required for some subsystems; Redwood Private in EU region discussed.
- SE notes: requested we include kernel selection guarantees for long-context models and show p95 with and without KV caching. Also flagged GPU family mapping: they want A100-80GB equivalent for large context LLMs and lower-memory GPUs for embedding-only pools.
- Quote from VP Eng: "We need an apples-to-apples cost model — show us the per-token economics, with sensitivity to utilization and model mix."
- Action items assigned: SE to deliver a refined cost spreadsheet with per-token breakouts (tokens by workload type, amortized GPU, infra, ops), AE to get procurement cadence, security to escalate HSM options.
- Stubs: fireflies ids and drive links added above.
commercial_notes: Negotiation levers: commit length (12 vs 36 months), burst allowances, reserved GPU family, SLA targets (p95 latency & availability), overage pricing, annual rightsizing credits. Finance prefers blended price guarantees for token bands and opt-in credits if utilization falls below 50%.
technical_requirements_summary: Must support VPC peering, private control plane, HSM-backed KMS, audit logs streamed to customer SIEM. Latency SLOs measured at app ingress; require tracing hooks. Prefer model pinning + canary rollout capability. Need automated batching/caching tuning and visibility into per-route token breakdowns.
